confirmedFixes.problem: YouTube media Next/Previous/Skip keys were blocked while Related, Comments or Description was open.
confirmedFixes.correction: Let the nine global media keys continue through existing regular/Shorts/live dispatch while native panels keep D-pad ownership.

confirmedFixes.problem: A stale attached stream holder could cache old metadata after commit, then Refresh renewed links/reordered sources and focused Alpha instead of the selected Beta.
confirmedFixes.correction: Memoize semantic labels from the canonical committed Stream with an identity guard; leave unmatched old holders uncached.

harnessCorrections.evidence: Original test did not establish dialog window focus, successful newer focus or actual root input. Strengthened matched-root/window/readiness case and trace pass unchanged production; the original precise cause remains unobserved. NativeUi was not changed.

Original test did not establish attached Watch/first-frame/window/focus readiness. Strengthened trace proves queue/decoder survive trim, key is delivered/handled, next route precedes decoder replacement, and Back restores Shorts. No model/queue fix was made.

Fixture control reset does not clear cumulative portal_links; the previous navigation test explicitly tuned once. Corrected audit preserves absolute counts and requires zero added links per profile, Live setup/input and whole measured journey. The passing combined rerun started/ended at cumulative 15 and added zero.

Test setup replaced the fixture model while coalescing routes, leaving the old view with a new inactive model. The corrected test signs in through the current model using the existing fixture OAuth flow, then actually checks unchanged-source epoch revocation and a fresh explicit Play.

First attempt stopped at a held-layout FocusFinder setup assertion before the suspected defect. Explicitly focusing the validated old holder reached the genuine external wrong-source failure in the next job; that bug was then fixed and its Play/Back/header checks pass.

infrastructureNotes.classification: Build dependency download failure before instrumentation on a replaced/cold worker; not an application-test failure.
Worker replaced before artifact collection; no final pass claimed. CLI retry and later final playback batch provide collected results.
Worker replaced after APK chunk upload; missing blob before instrumentation. Reuploaded and repeated the affected batch.

infrastructureNotes.workaround: Private runner verifies 153 source hashes and a checksum/signature-verified locally built APK pair. Six authenticated sub-4MiB immutable chunks avoid Maven and upload-size failures. No signing keys or application data were uploaded; root tracked runner/dependencies were unchanged.

historicalIsolatedNavigationComparison.scope: Historical isolated navigation comparison before the two later QA fixes. The scrolling/cache design is unchanged; these are not physical-TV timings or a universal final-build frame-rate claim.

finalMainNavigationMeasurements.scope: Final main APK in a broader warm QA process. All seven destinations and no-decoder assertions passed; the final absolute-zero cumulative counter assertion was invalid and corrected separately. Do not treat its PSS versus an isolated baseline as a causal memory delta.

reviews: Independent whole-app QA inventory, exact 275-case reconciliation, failure triage and native visual review.

Independent state/cache review and real refreshed-source regression through Play, headers and Back.
Native captures reviewed across all three areas, player HUD/storyboards/Description; no visual blocker found.
limitations: No TCL/physical-TV playback, performance, remote hardware or audible-output acceptance was performed.
Actual Google owner approval, account mutations/history acceptance, real phone pairing and private IPTV streams were not exercised; their regression paths use generated fixtures.
Anonymous live-service check covers Home/library only, not real stream playback or Google pairing.

Worker SwiftShader timings include jank and scheduling variability. Historical isolated and final broad-process memory samples have different warmup/state; they do not prove TV frame pacing, a universal latency improvement or a fixed whole-process memory increase.
